name: Abram
overview: Abram, a male figure known as the son of Terah (GEN 11:26), is a foundational patriarch in biblical history. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is recognized primarily through his familial and covenantal roles. No additional notes are provided to elaborate on his background.
namesAndTitles: The name Abram means 'exalted father' and was his original proper name (GEN 11:27). God later gave him the name Abraham, meaning 'father of many' (GEN 17:5), highlighting his role as the progenitor of a great nation. He is also referred to by divine titles such as 'My servant Abraham' (GEN 26:24), 'Abraham My friend' (IS 41:8), and 'friend of God' (JAS 2:23), which emphasize his special relationship with God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Abram as the son of Terah and husband to Sarai (GEN 11:26, GEN 11:29). He had a concubine named Hagar with whom he fathered Ishmael (GEN 16:2, GEN 16:16), and through Sarai, he fathered Isaac (GEN 17:19). Later, he married Keturah and fathered several sons including Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, and Midian (GEN 25:1-2). He also had allies named Mamre, Aner, and Eshcol (GEN 14:13), and Eliezer was his original heir (GEN 15:2). Sarai is also noted as his half-sister (GEN 20:12).
scriptureSignificance: Abram, later named Abraham by God, is a central figure in the biblical narrative as the recipient of God's covenant promising numerous descendants and the establishment of a great nation. His faith and obedience in responding to God's call to leave his homeland and trust in divine promises mark him as a model believer. Through his son Isaac, the covenantal promise continued, and Abraham's legacy as the father of the Hebrew nation and an exemplar of faith remains foundational for understanding God's redemptive plan culminating in Christ.
